source.method: yt-dlp flat channel enumeration + oEmbed identity sweep + LLM title-to-spec adjudication; evidence is TITLE-ONLY (no high rows); tightened binding rule (title must name the spec's distinctive content); sewage filter applied (promo/announcement/non-teaching uploads excluded)

review.task: T-VIDEOMAP-P4 (shelf-direct lane, Cognito maths shelf: igcse-maths-b-16)
review.ruling: delegated self-review — owner chat 2026-11-09: 'For now, approve and review yourself'
review.reviewer: delegated self-review (agent, per owner chat 2026-11-09: 'approve and review yourself')
review.evidenceBasis: Checked every mapping row of the 107-row draft against the igcse-maths-b-16 (4MB1) spine, judging each (video,spec) pair independently — including the umbrella specs (1A, 6A, 7A) and the physics-branded vector rows, which were kept only where the title names the spec's own clause (e.g. 'Find Resultant' for 8H, 'Scalar & Vector Quantities' for 8A). Rejected 1 spec-level binding: 'Similar Shapes' off 6H, where the evidence itself marks proof of similarity 'only supporting'. All other low rows name a clause genuinely in the spec (midpoint→4H coordinates, regular polygons→6C, fraction-of-a-number→1H).

rejects.reason: 'Similar Shapes' names the similarity domain (6G's 'Similarity: areas and volumes of similar figures' survives on that head topic), but 6H's distinctive frame is 'Prove the similarity of two triangles' — proof work and the SSS/SAS/ASA/RHS-style conditions are not title-evidenced, and the evidence itself concedes proof is 'only supporting'. Ride-along on the 6G binding; rejected at medium.
